why: Rule 1 at a deg-3 junction: 10 cm proton Braggs away to 168k at 11003, hot 2.4 cm pi+ stub, and the 66 cm muon leaves and rises to its own stop at 11000/11006.
Rule 1 clean: both prongs rise away (26 cm proton x2.03 to 216k, 125 cm muon x1.78), 93 deg opening so not the collinear trap, and it is the low-z end.
Rule 8: the whole event is four isolated sub-cm blobs with no segment, no direction and no readable topology, so any click is as good as another.
Degree-7 star in the zoom: stopping proton to 15001, stopping pi+ rising away x2.02 to 15006, plus the 212 cm muon leaving forward; textbook multi-prong vertex.

Neither end Braggs (the 19000 end is one 175k point dropping to MIP in 2 cm), so no stopping end exists; 19000 is the only interior endpoint, its blob reading as vertex charge, while 19001 sits in the y wall.
Deg-3 junction where the 18 cm proton rises away x1.34 to 132k at 13004 and the 204 cm pion rises away x1.97 to its stop at 13000.
The 147 cm track has a monotone Bragg to 280k at 7001, so it starts at the cool interior end 7002, which also carries a short e stub and nearby blobs.
Rule 1 with 2 of 2 rising away: 48 cm proton x2.23 to 189k at 13004 and 172 cm muon x1.62 forward; the muon later stops with a Michel-like stub at 13007.
Kink where the 9.6 cm proton rises away to 172k at 5001 while the 110 cm muon leaves and exits the x wall; several vertex blobs sit within 15 cm.
Deg-3 junction with two very hot short protons (114k and 260k) pointing away plus a 28 cm track rising away x1.72 to its stop at 17001.
Hot 6.4 cm stopping proton at 11002 with the 401 cm muon rising away x1.78 to a Bragg at 11000, where two small clusters sit as a Michel (rule 3 far end).
Deg-7 star: 36 cm proton rises away x2.59 to 213k at 10002, three pions rise away, and the 312 cm muon leaves; the zoom shows a clean multi-prong hub.
Two clusters start 2.7 cm apart at z about 2: the 134 cm track (rises away x5.04) and a 12 cm proton stopping at 170k; 8001 is the muon start of that V.
V apex with a dense charge blob read hot by both prongs, the 312 cm muon running forward to a Bragg at 15000, lowest z, and small satellite clusters around it.
Very fragmented shower event; 109123 is the lowest-z deg-4 hub with 2 prongs rising away and a shower-like cone, but the 50 cm Bragg proton starts 50 cm away at 109168.
